summary.text: Richard Neal is the Democratic incumbent for Massachusetts's 1st District, a former Springfield high school teacher, city councilor and mayor who has served in the U.S. House since 1989.
He chaired the House Ways and Means Committee from 2019 to 2023 and is now its ranking Democrat; he won the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary and is seeking another term.

paragraphs.text: Neal was born in Worcester, Massachusetts, in 1949 and was raised and educated in Springfield.

He earned a bachelor's degree in political science from American International College and a master's degree in public administration from the Barney School of Business and Public Administration at the University of Hartford.
He worked as a high school teacher and, beginning in 1973, as an assistant to Springfield Mayor William C. Sullivan.
Neal was elected to the Springfield City Council in 1978 and served as Mayor of Springfield from 1984 to 1988.
He was first elected to the U.S. House in 1988 and represented Massachusetts's 2nd District from 1989 to 2013 and the redrawn 1st District since then.
After two terms on the House Banking Committee, he joined the Ways and Means Committee in 1993.

Elected its chairman in January 2019, he held the post until 2023 and has been its ranking member since January 2023; his official biography describes his chairmanship as the first by a Massachusetts representative since 1875.
Neal is the Democratic leader of the Friends of Ireland Caucus and, according to his official biography, traveled to Ireland in 1994 to observe the first IRA ceasefire.

His official biography also describes him as dean of the Massachusetts and New England congressional delegations and lists honorary degrees from institutions including Mount Holyoke College, Springfield College, Ulster University and Queen's University Belfast.
